nodes.description: Biallelic truncating BLVRA variants abolish biliverdin reductase A. The Inuit founder variant c.214C>A (p.Ser44Ter) produces a truncated protein with no catalytic activity when expressed in human hepatoma cells and Xenopus oocytes. BVR-A is ubiquitously expressed and is the predominant biliverdin reductase isoenzyme in adults.

evidence.snippet: Immunoblotting, immunofluorescence and functional assays of BVRα activity revealed that the mutated sequence generates a truncated protein with no catalytic activity.

Biliary obstruction (in the Inuit cases) or decompensated cirrhosis (in the Swedish case) is the precipitant. In the absence of cholestasis BVR-A deficiency is clinically silent: a homozygous sister of one proband never had hyperbiliverdinemia or cholestasis, and the green discoloration disappeared after surgical correction of the obstruction. The crises were accompanied by raised biochemical markers of cholestasis and hypercholanemia.

nodes.description: Heme oxygenase converts heme to iron, carbon monoxide and biliverdin IXalpha, which BVR-A then reduces to bilirubin IXalpha. With BVR-A absent, heme catabolism stops at biliverdin. In healthy individuals circulating biliverdin is very low to undetectable because this reduction is efficient.
